summary: Open-weight and price competition led AI: Reflection AI's 501B Beam and Mistral Large 4 landed alongside Anthropic's $0.10/M Claude Haiku 5.5, and Google previewed a persistent enterprise Gemini agent. OpenAI's release of 372 AI-generated math result families (and withdrawal of three Hodge papers) sparked a 'Math 2.0' debate led by Terence Tao, with Daniel Litt as a new voice. In bio, Novartis paid $575M upfront for Abogen's mRNA-encoded T-cell engager, the Nobel in Medicine went to optogenetics, Paradromics reported 4+ years of stable recording, and Kyverna neared the first autoimmune CAR-T BLA. Waymo closed a $5B debt raise, Boston Dynamics named Rohit Prasad CEO, and a Jülich benchmark put Quantinuum ahead on QEC-style mid-circuit measurement.

highlights.title: 'Math 2.0': mathematicians say mass AI problem-solving forces a rethink
highlights.detail: Oct 6-8, 2026: Terence Tao said OpenAI's mass release ends 'Math 1.0' and called for a 'Math 2.0' valuing exposition and community; Daniel Litt was optimistic; an Association for Human Mathematics letter urged mathematicians to stop working with OpenAI; Tristan Buckmaster questioned due diligence and Andrew Sutherland said single-agent claims are unverified.

payload.thesis: When AI can mass-solve open problems, math must re-value exposition and direction-setting, and labs need disclosure norms (prompts, compute, formalization).

highlights.title: Daniel Litt: Toronto mathematician, the optimist on AI-driven math
